risk_assessment.rationale: The alert aligns with the T1566 phishing pattern (executive impersonation) and includes 19 scanning‑type indicators from an unknown source, supporting a high‑severity assessment with medium confidence because of limited domain reputation data.

recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Immediately isolate the email from all internal mail streams and block any further delivery to the victim’s mailbox until a thorough forensic review is completed.

Perform a deep packet inspection on the inbound traffic associated with IP 185.220.101.47 to confirm whether it originates from a known malicious infrastructure or if it has been spoofed; consider blocking the IP at the perimeter firewall if it proves suspicious.

Conduct a reverse‑lookup and WHOIS audit of the domains cfo.support, secure‑invoice‑updates.com, jane.tan, and victimcorp.com to uncover any shared hosting providers, registrars, or previous abuse reports that could provide additional context.

Deploy an email authentication scan (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) against the sender’s domain to verify whether legitimate mail flow is possible; if the records are missing or misconfigured, flag this as a potential spoofing vector.

Engage the internal security operations team to run a sandbox analysis on any attachments or embedded links that were present in the message (even if not yet opened) to detect malicious payloads or phishing landing pages.
Notify the victim’s IT and HR departments of the impersonation attempt, providing them with guidance on how to verify legitimate CFO communications (e.g., direct phone call, separate email channel).
Add the sender’s IP and domain to a temporary blocklist in Mimecast while the investigation proceeds, ensuring that any future attempts are quarantined automatically.

Schedule a post‑incident review meeting with stakeholders to assess whether additional controls—such as mandatory two‑factor authentication for invoice approvals or stricter email filtering rules—are warranted.
